rules.definition: A spell_linked_spell on-remove cast (negative trigger, positive target) runs for every remove mode except AURA_REMOVE_BY_DEATH; an on-remove removal (negative target) runs for all modes.
rules.name: linked-on-remove-cast-suppressed-by-death

population.name: all: triggers with positive on-remove targets

rules.definition: A LINK_AURA child is created by caster->AddAura with its own duration (only if the caster exists), is removed with the parent's remove mode (same caster GUID only), and has its stack amount forced to the parent's on every parent stack change/refresh.
rules.name: linked-aura-bounded-by-parent-not-sharing-lifetime

population.name: all: LINK_AURA triggers with positive children

rules.definition: On apply, spell_area/linked cascades run before the aura's own effect handlers and OnEffectApply/AfterEffectApply scripts; on removal, the aura's effect handlers and OnEffectRemove/AfterEffectRemove scripts run first and the cascades last.
rules.name: external-cascade-ordering

rules.definition: An AuraScript OnEffectApply/AfterEffectApply/OnEffectRemove/AfterEffectRemove handler runs on a refresh or stack change iff its registration mask contains AURA_EFFECT_HANDLE_REAPPLY (or CHANGE_AMOUNT and the recomputed amount differs); REAL-only handlers do not.
rules.name: reapply-mode-handlers-run-on-refresh

population.name: all: apply/remove hook bindings with REAPPLY

rules.definition: Initial and max proc charges are spell_proc.Charges when that column is nonzero, else DB2 ProcCharges (then ProcCharges spell mods).
rules.name: spell-proc-charges-override

population.name: all: spells whose merged spell_proc charges differ from DB2 ProcCharges

counterexamples: not a proof: creature/instance/areatrigger scripts and non-literal engine branches are not indexed (AL-U-H-02)
rules.definition: Most aura providers have no external lifecycle touch in any indexed source; for those, every surface is decided by DB2 through the generic consumer (subject to the coverage caveat).

rules.definition: External removal behaviour may branch on the remove mode (EXPIRE, DEATH, ENEMY_SPELL, CANCEL, INTERRUPT, DEFAULT); death is a distinct input, never equal to expiry.
rules.name: remove-mode-is-observable-to-external-policy
